chapterGroups.title: The Trade
description: What a blacksmith's shop actually is, which is a pile of
iron and a person who has decided to be patient with it.

chapters.title: Toolsmith
chapters.subtitle: Branches, a repeatable job, and a hoard

quests.title: Iron, Twice
quests.subtitle: The first one is a lesson
description: Three ingots. The first one teaches you to make a furnace,
the second teaches you to stand next to it, and the third
is the one you get to keep.

quests.title: Something to Hit With
description: Four sticks is a hammer, apparently,
and this is the last time a crafting recipe will surprise you.

quests.title: The Blade
quests.subtitle: One of these two, not both
description: Two quests here share an exclusive group, so finishing one
locks the other for good. The lock is deliberate and it is
the only unrecoverable decision in this chapter --
/tasked reset clears it if you want to try the other.

quests.title: The Tools
quests.subtitle: The other one
description: The pickaxe instead of the sword. Cheaper to maintain,
less good at being a sword.

quests.title: Stoke the Fire
quests.subtitle: Repeatable, with a cooldown
description: A hexagonal node with a cooldown ring around it.
Four coal every two minutes, forever -- which is not much,
and is the point: a repeatable job should pay for the walk.
The shape is a hint about what a node is. Nothing enforces it;
a file can draw a repeatable quest as anything at all.
The icon is at iconScale 0.55, so it sits smaller in its node
than the quests around it -- which is how a minor, repeatable
job is told apart from a one-off milestone at a glance.

quests.title: One of the Two Above
quests.subtitle: minRequired, so either branch will do
description: This quest needs one of its two dependencies, not both --
because the two above are mutually exclusive and requiring
both would make this quest impossible.
minRequired is how an OR-gate is written. It wins over the
chapter's prerequisite mode, which is why setting it makes
the mode irrelevant here.

quests.title: One Thing at a Time
quests.subtitle: Sequential tasks
description: Two checkmarks, and the second one cannot be handed in
until the first is done. Open the quest and the Submit
button moves down to task two, because the first is behind it.
Sequential tasks are how an order matters. Without the flag
the two could be handed in in either order, or both at once.

quests.title: Curiosity
quests.subtitle: One required task, one that is not
description: The glass is required. The checkmark under it is optional --
a bonus for reading, which the quest itself does not need.
An optional task is still a button while it is undone, and
still counts towards nothing. If every task in a quest were
optional, any one of them would complete it.

quests.title: The Hoard
quests.subtitle: Invisible until you have it
description: You cannot see this node until the quest is complete.
Sort by chapter and there will be a gap where it sits,
which is the honest thing for a hidden quest to do --
a hidden node that leaves no gap tells you where it is.
iconScale 0.95, the other end of the range from the forge
above: nearly the whole node, because a hoard should look
like it is overflowing the thing holding it.
